what: Evaluation error of the 0.2 (60759d3) scoring of --param_dtype bf16 runs: the whole model, including the cross-entropy, ran in bf16 and each 64-window batch loss was rounded to bf16. 0.3 scores a bf16-weight model as an fp32 copy of its bf16 weights.
method: Checkpoints of results/published/save_muon_base_repro.json (fp32-trained, same model and data as the bf16 runs) cast to bf16, then scored on the same first-N val windows by bantamtrain.cli.pretrain.evaluate() of 60759d3 (bf16 math) and of 0.3 (fp32 math). bf16_math_error = 0.2 score - 0.3 score on identical bf16 weights.
conclusion: The bf16-math error is not a fixed offset: it is rounding noise of a few 1e-3 whose sign varies (+0.0007 at 2048 windows, -0.0035..-0.0005 at 1024, +0.0067 at 256). Rounding the weights to bf16 changes the loss by < 1e-4. So full_muon8_bf16 (2048 windows, 2.7280) is uncertain by about +-0.001 and lm_muon8_bf16 (1024 windows, 3.5752) by about +-0.004; neither bf16-trained model was saved, so neither can be re-scored, and both need a rerun.
caveat: Measured on an fp32-trained model rounded to bf16, not on the bf16-trained models themselves.
script: for each checkpoint: build_model(run args), load the state dict, then evaluate(model) and evaluate(copy.deepcopy(model).to(torch.bfloat16)) with a CPU runtime (no autocast), once with the 60759d3 package on sys.path and once with 0.3
